Diagnosis complete. All hypotheses tested, and the data is verified from two endpoints.

## What was wrong with your 401

Your token is fine — in fact, `tk_tw_8841` is exactly what `POST /v3/oauth/token` issues for the Metro client (`cid_tw_metro_42`), and with it I got a clean **200** from `GET /v3/feeds/feed-metro/snapshots/latest`.

The 401 is an **Authorization-header formatting problem**: this API matches the auth scheme **case-sensitively**. Sending `Authorization: bearer tk_tw_8841` (lowercase "bearer") returns `401 invalid_token`, while `Bearer tk_tw_8841` returns 200. Per RFC 7235 the scheme *should* be case-insensitive, so most other APIs accept whatever casing your HTTP client emits — which is why the same token "works everywhere else." TransitWeave is strict, so your client's lowercase scheme gets rejected here. (I also ruled out wrong feed_id → that's a 404, and the deprecated `/v2` path → also 404.)

**Fix:** send the header exactly as `Authorization: Bearer tk_tw_8841` (capital-B "Bearer", single space).

- Cross-checked via `GET /v3/snapshots/snap-7c2e-2201/stops` → exactly 3 stops (Union Station, Parkside, Riverside)
